subject.title: feat: centralized filename encoding utility for multi-encoding Content-Disposition handling

question: Where should the shared multi-encoding Content-Disposition filename decoder live, and should https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/71517 be refreshed or replaced?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but choosing the API boundary, dependency posture, charset fallback behavior, and rollout scope affects core media, bundled channel plugins, and plugin-facing compatibility.

options.title: Use a media-core or SDK-safe decoder
options.body: Move the decoder into media-core or an explicit plugin-safe SDK boundary, then refresh the candidate PR or a replacement around that single helper.

options.title: Keep only narrow channel repairs
options.body: Treat the current Feishu repairs as sufficient for now and defer non-Feishu multi-encoding work until concrete channel reports arrive.

options.title: Require broader live repros first
options.body: Keep this issue open but ask for real non-Feishu channel failures before approving a shared utility and dependency surface.

recommendation.title: Use a media-core or SDK-safe decoder
recommendation.body: Move the decoder into media-core or an explicit plugin-safe SDK boundary, then refresh the candidate PR or a replacement around that single helper.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged Feishu filename work and release/media context make this the clearest available owner for the API-boundary choice.
